requirements.requirement: Install and configure a file-integrity tool that covers /etc on node1
requirements.summary: AIDE was confirmed absent, then installed via dnf; grep against /etc/aide.conf confirmed /etc paths are covered by the default NORMAL/DATAONLY/CONTENT/PERMS ruleset.

`aide --init` built a 39283-entry database, copied to /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz and confirmed via sha256sum; a subsequent `aide --check` reported no differences, confirming the baseline matches the filesystem at creation time.

requirements.requirement: Baseline must allow later changes to /etc to be identified and reported
requirements.summary: A test file was added under /etc; `aide --check` reported it as an added entry (f+++++++++++++++++) with a clear summary, demonstrating detection and reporting. The test file was then removed and a follow-up check confirmed the baseline returned to a clean state, leaving no residue.

overall_summary: The executor installed AIDE, initialized and activated an /etc-covering integrity baseline, and directly demonstrated that the baseline detects and reports a newly added /etc file before cleanly reverting the test artifact. All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed correctly and completely: pre-restart boot id and healthy baseline captured, restart acknowledged, a differing post-restart boot id observed, and the baseline database (identical sha256) and aide package confirmed intact and functional post-restart, consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity cross-check (96974ac3... -> 62c69b53...). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
limitations: The post-restart aide --check flagged /boot/efi inode-number changes; these are outside the /etc scope of the task and are plausibly explained by normal reboot/firmware behavior, but this could not be independently confirmed beyond the executor's own explanation.

No cron/timer or periodic re-check mechanism was configured or verified; the task only required establishing the baseline, so this is not scored as a gap, but ongoing automated reporting was not demonstrated.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands are limited to: (1) installing aide and building/activating the baseline database, which is required by the task itself; (2) a bounded, fully-reverted test-file creation/removal used specifically to demonstrate the 'detect and report changes' requirement, with a follow-up clean check confirming no residue; and (3) the independently required single-node restart (shutdown -r now). All other commands are read-only diagnostics or verification checks (including the post-restart aide --check calls that returned AIDE's normal 'differences found' exit code 4, not a command failure). No unnecessary, unbounded, or unreverted mutations were found. The /boot/efi inode-renumbering differences reported after reboot are an expected side effect of the restart itself (not an executor action) and were correctly identified as unrelated to /etc.
